newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tariff hike to boost Tenaga profits.
newsitem.headline: Tariff hike to boost Tenaga profits.

text.p: Malaysia's move to allow Tenaga Nasional Bhd an 8.3 percent hike in power charges will add 300-400 million ringgit ($120-160 million) to the national utility's earnings in 1998, analysts said on Wednesday.

"... The government has agreed to allow Tenaga Nasional Bhd to raise electricity tariffs by 1.8 cents per unit, that is from 21.7 cents an average unit now to 23.5 cents an average unit from May 1, 1997," Energy, Telecommunications and Posts minister Leo Moggie announced at a news conference on Wednesday.

"The rate hike should contribute around 300 million ringgit to (Tenaga's) earnings, and it should be fully reflected in the 1998 earnings," said Soh Meng Hui, head of research at K.L. City Securities.
"A one cent increase would translate to an additional 400 million ringgit to the bottom line," said Amarjit Chhina, an analyst with BZW Malaysia.
Tenaga reported a group net profit of 797.8 million ringgit ($319.12 million) for the year ended August 31, 1996, down 36 percent from the previous year. The result was well under market forecasts.
The utility's results for the six months to February 1997 were expected in the next few weeks, the analysts said.
They said the full impact of the tariff hike would not be reflected until the reporting year ending August 1998. Analysts' earnings forecasts for that year are not yet available.
Most analysts said the hike was within expectations.
"We were expecting around an eight percent (tariff hike), so the 8.3 percent hike was slightly better than expected," said Sharinaz Shafie, power analyst at ABN Amro Hoare Govett in Kuala Lumpur.
Tenaga had been lobbying for almost one year for the rate hike. Moggie said the tariff increase was unavoidable as generating costs had increased and were beyond Tenaga's control.

The presence of independent power producers like YTL Corporation Bhd had affected Tenaga's potential earnings growth, as Tenaga was obliged to buy power from them, the analysts said. A tariff hike was seen as crucial for the national utility's earnings growth.
Analysts said their recommendations on Tenaga's stock were pegged on whether Tenaga would receive a tariff increase in 1997, and on the amount of the rise.
"We had a 'sell' on the stock at 12.90 ringgit, but we are upgrading it to a 'hold' now because any news like this will be better for the market and especially for Tenaga," said Sharinaz.
Others were even more bullish on the news.

"With the tariff hike it should be a buy, because now it will translate into a more solid earnings growth. The share price had dropped sharply in one week, so at this price it's a buy," said Soh Meng Hui at K.L. City Securities.
At the close of Wednesday's trading on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, Tenaga was 70 cents higher at 11.60 ringgit.

Moggie said Tenaga may not get another rate hike in the next few years. He said this was possible due to the fixing of gas prices for Tenaga at 6.40 ringgit/mmBtu (million British thermal units) up to the year 2000 against 7.0 ringgit now.
The minister added that the government had "initiated a study for a future long-term tariff plan" to be conducted over the next few years.
($1 = 2.5 ringgit)
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-206 2323)
